newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says electronic money impact on policy limited.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says electronic money impact on policy limited.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Friday that the introduction of electronic money in Japan would be unlikely to have a large impact on the effectiveness of the central bank's monetary policy.

"We think the possibility that the effectiveness of (the central bank's) monetary policy will be greatly affected is small, unless electronic money replaces paper money and deposits not only in small settlements but in large ones as well," he said in a speech.

The use of electronic money may have some impact on money-related data, such as money supply, but the bank would deal with any problems by determining the amount of electronic money in circulation and by shrewd monetary policy management, he said.

In his speech to business leaders about Japan's settlement system, Matsushita said that the central bank would provide the necessary funds to address systemic risks, while monitoring the settlement system daily.
It will also keep watch over the business of individual private banks, he said.

He said that the banking sector is different from other sectors because it is part of a settlement network where systemic risk exists. Should one bank fail to honour its payments, this could trigger a chain reaction that could cause the whole system to come crashing down, he said.
Since the settlement system is supported largely by factors such as credibility, there is also a risk that one bank's failure could affect the deposits of other banks, he added.

As a way to secure the stability and ensure the safety of the nation's settlement system, the BOJ plans to introduce a real-time gross settlement system (RTGS) by the year 2000. This will allow financial firms to settle transactions on a real-time basis, whereas under the current system, transactions are settled at four specific times during the day, he said.
The central bank is ready to provide the necessary liquidity for the smooth implementation of the RTGS, he added.
Besides the implementation of the real-time system, Matsushita also called on private clearing systems to work towards ensuring stability of the settlement system.
